title: The Crusade
author: Brady V.
desc: This program aimed at mainly intermediates and some novices that can still work for advanced lifters,is designed to get you generally strong,pack on muscle,and teach you ways to progress your training throughout the rest of your lifting career using clusters,back off sets,and things like dynamic double progression with tried and true movements done with a 5 day a week,upper,lower,full split,this program can be run indefinitely and use one week deloads as you see fit depending on recovery and how advanced you are,you can use any variation of the compounds I list you like if you want or re run it but that’s your choice

ex.note: The reason I listed rpe is these amraps are as many good reps as you can get and on the first set you’re aiming for 5 reps then from there drop 15% and 25%,if you get a +2 on top set add 5lbs nextweek
On this follow a dynamic double progression or aim for one end of rep range and follow LP
Same rules as leg curl,but on these don’t stand up all the way and get a short pause at bottom
2 sets of 1 minute cable crunch focus on basically going to failure with perfect form
Same rules as leg curl
Same rules from day 1 squats
Dynamic double progression and perfect form,highly recommend straps or versa Gripps,these should be quite hard if done correctly,if you don’t have enough weight Meadows Row is a viable option
Same rules as rows minus the grip
Any fly is a good substitute but ideally use the pec deck,very slow good stretch and squeeze
Push these enough to establish a little pump and warm the elbows up
Ez bar is acceptable and I recommend doing these from a decline,1 count pause at bottom
Use around a 30 degree incline and be as strict as you can be with these and use a regular double progression
Same rules as squats and Larsen press
3 sets really heavy don’t be sloppy but not super strict and 4th set 3 count hold at top and bottom,dynamic double progression
Stimulate don’t annihilate
Set a timer for 1 minute and really squeeze in as much work as you can whatever you means you can without getting sloppy
Really milk as much as you can on these,3rd set should exhaust everything out of you
As many good reps as you can squeeze in,weighted with dynamic double is permissible and assisted if you need it
Dynamic double progression or LP,3rd set should be closest to failure but technique should be pure
No momentum,1 count hold at top,ideally do these seated but standing is okay too
Same rules as squats
Incredibly strict no momentum,very slow,full rotation and extension,no resting between each rep
Use these to really overload those biceps,ideally dynamic double progression
Really pump blood into those rear delts control it but not a crazy slow tempo but you’re not explosive
Same rules as day 1 squat
Dynamic double progression and incredibly strict form to prevent from overloading your spine
Emphasize the stretch and squeeze stimulate don’t annihilate
